import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import TfidfVectorizer
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.metrics import log_loss
import os
import re
from scipy.sparse import hstack

# Read data from input directory
train_df = pd.read_csv("input/train.csv")
test_df = pd.read_csv("input/test.csv")

# Load sample submission for format reference
sample_sub = pd.read_csv("input/sample_submission.csv")


# Text preprocessing function with comprehensive cleaning
def preprocess_text(text):
    text = str(text).lower()
    # Remove HTML tags, quotes, parentheses, brackets
    text = re.sub(r'[<>"()\[\]{}]', " ", text)
    # Keep only letters and alphanumeric
    text = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9\s]", " ", text)
    # Normalize multiple spaces to single space
    text = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", text).strip()
    return text


# Apply preprocessing to all texts
X_train_cleaned = train_df["text"].apply(preprocess_text)
X_test_cleaned = test_df["text"].apply(preprocess_text)

# Train-test split strategy: keep original training labels, validate separately
y_train = train_df["author"].map({"EAP": 0, "HPL": 1, "MWS": 2}).values

# Create stratified train/validation split using cleaned text
X_train_val, X_test_holdout, y_train_val, y_test_holdout = train_test_split(
    X_train_cleaned.values, y_train, test_size=0.2, random_state=42, stratify=y_train
)

# Combine with character n-gram features for better author detection
char_vectorizer = TfidfVectorizer(
    analyzer="char", ngram_range=(1, 3), max_features=15000, min_df=1, sublinear_tf=True
)
X_char_train = char_vectorizer.fit_transform(X_train_cleaned.to_numpy())
X_char_holdout = char_vectorizer.transform(X_test_holdout.to_numpy())

# Create word-level TF-IDF with bigrams
word_vectorizer = TfidfVectorizer(
    max_features=12000, ngram_range=(1, 2), min_df=2, sublinear_tf=True
)
X_word_train = word_vectorizer.fit_transform(X_train_cleaned.to_numpy())
X_word_holdout = word_vectorizer.transform(X_test_holdout.to_numpy())

# Combine word and character features for final representation
X_train_combined = hstack([X_word_train, X_char_train])
X_test_holdout_combined = hstack([X_word_holdout, X_char_holdout])

# Train model with optimized hyperparameters
clf = LogisticRegression(
    C=2.0, max_iter=5000, class_weight="balanced", random_state=42, solver="lbfgs"
)
clf.fit(X_train_combined, y_train_val)

# Compute hold-out validation metric (genuine estimate)
log_loss_val = log_loss(y_test_holdout, clf.predict_proba(X_test_holdout_combined))
print(f"Validation Log Loss (Hold-out): {log_loss_val:.4f}")

# Make predictions on full test set
X_test_combined = hstack(
    [
        word_vectorizer.transform(test_df["text"].apply(preprocess_text)),
        char_vectorizer.transform(test_df["text"].apply(preprocess_text)),
    ]
)
y_pred_prob = clf.predict_proba(X_test_combined)

# Clip probabilities to avoid numerical issues
y_pred_scaled = np.clip(y_pred_prob, 1e-15, 1 - 1e-15)

# Normalize rows so they sum to 1
y_pred_norm = y_pred_scaled / np.sum(y_pred_scaled, axis=1, keepdims=True)

# Ensure submission directory exists
os.makedirs("submission", exist_ok=True)

# Prepare submission dataframe matching required column order
submission_df = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "id": test_df["id"].values,
        "EAP": y_pred_norm[:, 0],
        "HPL": y_pred_norm[:, 1],
        "MWS": y_pred_norm[:, 2],
    }
)

# Save to required location
submission_df.to_csv("submission/submission.csv", index=False)
print("Submission saved successfully to submission/submission.csv")
